summary: Iteration 136 — Backend security regression pass (SEC-001/SEC-002/SEC-003 cross-org denial + with_admin->with_org downgrades). 19/19 pytest passed against real Supabase Postgres over the preview URL. Verified end-to-end with a GENUINE second admin in a genuine second org (orgb-test-3628a11d@example.com in 'IDOR Test Org B' = 3628a11d-36b8-42df-9d46-0479450ee22c) vs admin@supervision.com in 'Test Company' (b00bf04f-a1b9-4673-8430-b4a08ba15d6c). SEC-001: DELETE /api/admin/standards/{id} — org-A admin against an org-B standard_id returns 404 AND the row stays is_active=TRUE (no silent side-effect); same admin deactivating own-org custom standard still returns 200 and flips is_active=FALSE. SEC-002 (all 4 endpoints): plain 'admin' role gets 404 on GET /api/admin/users/debug-by-email, GET /api/admin/users/{id}/debug, GET /api/admin/meetings/{id}/debug-attendees, POST /api/admin/meetings/{id}/add-attendee when the target user/meeting is in a different org; same admin gets 200 when target is in own org; super_admin (superadmin@1two.one) can still cross orgs freely. add-attendee also correctly 404s when the meeting is in-org but the target user is in a foreign org. SEC-003: GET /api/admin/export-cc-excerpts?staff_ids=<own,foreign> — foreign-org user id silently filtered out by RLS in with_org() (returned as either 200 PDF containing only own-org names, or 404 no-evidence — both prove the foreign id contributed zero meetings/names). Regressions verified: GET /api/admin/standards (list), POST /api/admin/standards (create) + DELETE (deactivate) round-trip, GET/PUT /api/admin/template, GET /api/admin/users, POST /api/review/{id}/rescan-evidence, POST /api/review/{id}/send-email — all work same-org with the with_org(org_id) downgrade, no behaviour change. Prep-questions endpoint GET /api/prep/{id} returns <500 (Python 3.11 syntax fix verified via non-crash + full 45-test suite requiring backend to be up).
critical_code_review_comments: admin.py::debug_by_email/debug_user/debug_meeting_attendees/repair_add_attendee all still use database.with_admin() to fetch and then apply an in-Python `if u["org_id"] != caller_org: raise 404` gate. This works, but it is a defence-in-depth REGRESSION vs the SEC-001 pattern (delete_standard uses with_org() so RLS filters at the SQL layer — a future refactor cannot accidentally bypass). Recommend: either (a) split the code path — do a with_org() existence probe first and only fall through to with_admin() when caller is super_admin, or (b) at minimum keep a unit test guarding the org_id-compare line so a future refactor that deletes the check gets caught in CI. The current pytest in this iteration exercises the runtime behaviour but does NOT guard the source line.

admin.py::repair_add_attendee — the SEC-002 gate rejects when EITHER the meeting is cross-org OR the target user is cross-org, both returning 'Meeting not found' 404. Silently misleading when only the user is cross-org (the meeting exists and belongs to the caller). Consider a distinct 400/404 message ('User not in your organisation') for auditability, since this is a repair endpoint used by real admins interactively.

admin.py::export_cc_excerpts — SEC-003 relies on RLS silently dropping foreign uuids from the `SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ANY($1::uuid[])` result. That's correct at the DB layer, but it means the caller gets NO feedback (200 with own-only staff_label, or 404 no-evidence) when they mistakenly paste a foreign id. Consider logging.warn('SEC-003: %d/%d staff_ids belonged to foreign org', dropped, total) so a real cross-org attempt is visible in security logs.

tests/reset_test_pw.py had a stale `now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()` that broke asyncpg's timestamptz encoder (fixed in-place this iteration — passed datetime object directly). Worth committing so next agent doesn't hit it.

memory/test_credentials.md claims superadmin@1two.one password is 'TestPass123!' but the DB had `supabase_password_set=TRUE` which routed auth through Supabase (where that password wasn't set), giving a 401. Had to flip supabase_password_set=FALSE + re-hash bcrypt to make the documented password work. Same trap probably still applies to alex@1two.one / hello@1two.one / sarah@supervision.com. Recommend a startup-time reconciliation check or clearer doc note that bcrypt fallback requires supabase_password_set=FALSE.
